answer: Commit-reveal integrity blocks copy identities. Each identity posts its plume-signed draft hash to a harbor board, locking a 50-credit bond; the hidden hash cannot be copied before writing. At reveal, raven auditors recompute each hash; a mismatch burns the bond. Post-reveal copies mismatch, and one draft under many identities exposes identical reveals, burning bonds. Each fake pays 25 for one draft plus 50 at risk; the k-th fake costs as much as the first, so 1,000 fakes cost 25,000 and risk 50,000. An honest identity pays 25 once, recovering its bond from the harbor board after a reveal.
